# Loui DS: full documentation

> Loui DS is a dark, minimal, functional React design system (React 19, React Aria Components, CSS Modules, DTCG tokens) for internal tools, dashboards and apps. It is built to be operated by humans and AI agents.

Rules for generated UI:

- Use only components, hooks and tokens exported by the package; never write raw colors, px sizes, z-indexes or inline styles.
- One primary action per screen (`Button variant="primary"`), top right. The accent blue is for focus, selection and links only.
- Hierarchy comes from surface plus border; shadows only on overlays.
- Color never carries meaning alone: pair it with text or an icon with a name.
- Every interactive element needs an accessible name; icon-only controls require a `label`.
- Microcopy: English, sentence case, buttons are verb + object, no exclamation marks, no emoji. See content-rules.json.
- No user-visible string literals in components: use the message catalog and `DSProvider`.
- Money is integer minor units plus an ISO 4217 code; format dates, numbers and money with the provided utilities.
- Do not use `experimental` or `deprecated` components in recipes or generated code unless the user asks.

---

## Getting started

### Requirements

- React 19 and React DOM 19 (peer dependencies). React 18 is not supported.
- An evergreen browser. Node 24 or later for tooling.
- A bundler that handles CSS imports and `woff2` assets (Vite, Next.js, webpack, esbuild).

### Install

`@loui/ds` is private and unlicensed for now (ADR-0004). Install it from your private registry or workspace:

```sh
pnpm add @loui/ds react react-dom
```

`react-aria-components`, `react-stately` and `lucide-react` are regular dependencies of the package; you do not install them yourself.

### 1. Load the stylesheet once

Import the stylesheet once, at the root of your app, before any component renders:

```tsx
import '@loui/ds/styles.css';
```

It contains, in this layer order, `reset`, `tokens`, `base`, `components` and `utilities`. Because everything sits in named cascade layers, your own unlayered CSS always wins over the design system without specificity tricks.

The stylesheet sets the dark theme on the page (`bg-canvas` on `html`, `bg` and `text` on `body`, the Geist font), so you normally do not need your own reset.

### 2. Wrap the app in `DSProvider`

```tsx
import { DSProvider } from '@loui/ds';

export function Root({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <DSProvider locale="en-US">{children}</DSProvider>;
}
```

| Prop       | Purpose                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`   | BCP 47 tag. Drives messages, number and date formatting, sorting, and the direction (RTL) of React Aria widgets. |
| `messages` | Overrides keyed by component, e.g. `{ Alert: { dismiss: 'Close' } }`. Applied over the built-in catalogs.        |
| `navigate` | Client-side navigation for `Link` and link-like components (your router's `navigate`).                           |
| `useHref`  | Maps a router path to a real `href` (needed for basename routing).                                               |

Without a provider everything still works in `en-US`; it just does not follow the user's locale. English is the default and `pt-BR` ships with the library. See `docs/architecture/i18n.md` for how messages resolve.

Client-side routing, for example with React Router:

```tsx
import { useNavigate, useHref } from 'react-router';

function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  return (
    <DSProvider navigate={navigate} useHref={useHref}>
      {children}
    </DSProvider>
  );
}
```

### 3. Use components

```tsx
import { Alert, Button } from '@loui/ds';

export function Example() {
  return (
    <>
      <Alert tone="warning" title="Low stock">
        3 rolls of linen are left. Reorder to avoid delays.
      </Alert>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={() => console.log('created')}>
        Create order
      </Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

Use `onPress`, not `onClick`: it is the React Aria press event and works for mouse, touch, keyboard and screen readers.

### Fonts

Geist (UI) and Geist Mono (data) are self-hosted and ship inside the package: `styles.css` references `./fonts/*.woff2` relative to itself, and the build copies them to `dist/fonts`. Nothing is fetched from Google Fonts or a CDN at runtime. Your bundler resolves the font files when it processes `@loui/ds/styles.css`; there is nothing to configure. Both families load with `font-display: swap` and a metric-matched fallback so the layout does not shift.

### Theming

Dark is the only theme. The semantic token layer (`--ds-bg`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, ...) can be overridden in your own CSS if you must; component code only reads semantic tokens. A `[data-theme="paper"]` scope provides the light surface for receipt and PDF previews. Forced-colors and reduced-motion modes are handled by the components.

### Server-side rendering

- Components never touch `window` or `document` while rendering or at import time, so they render on the server.
- IDs come from React `useId`; React Aria needs no `SSRProvider` with React 19.
- `useMediaQuery` returns its `defaultValue` (`false`) on the server and corrects after hydration. Prefer CSS media queries for styling.
- Import `@loui/ds/styles.css` in the root layout so the first paint is already styled.

### Framework notes

**Vite.** Import the stylesheet in `main.tsx`; nothing else is needed.

**Next.js (App Router).** Import the stylesheet in `app/layout.tsx` and render `DSProvider` in a small client component, because it takes functions as props. The package does not yet ship `'use client'` directives, so import interactive components from client components (a file with `'use client'`). This is tracked under REL-001 and not yet verified in a Next.js fixture.

### Next steps

- Read the [Principles](./principles.md) and the [Content guidelines](./content-guidelines.md) before building a screen.
- Browse the components in Storybook; each page lists props, variants, states and accessibility notes.
- Agents: start from [Using with AI](./using-with-ai.md).

---

## Principles

These rules apply to every screen built with Loui DS. They are short on purpose. When a case is not covered, choose the option that keeps the user's attention on one thing.

### Three rules

1. **One accent.** The blue accent (`--ds-accent`) is only for focus, selection, links and "open" states. Never use it for buttons or large fills.
2. **Ink for action.** The primary button is light on dark (`--ds-primary-bg`). Use **one primary action per screen**.
3. **Borders first.** Hierarchy comes from surface plus border. Shadows only on overlays: menus, toasts, dialogs and sheets.

### Clarity and focus

The system is designed for use that needs no effort of attention (the first product's owner has ADHD). Every new screen follows these rules.

1. **One main action per screen,** always at the top right, with a keyboard shortcut.
2. **The most important thing comes first and is largest.** Everything else is secondary text (`--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`).
3. **Color only carries meaning, and is always accompanied by text.** Never signal status by color alone.
4. **Fixed positions.** The same element lives in the same place in every module, with no misalignments: a 4 px grid and fixed heights.
5. **Deleting always asks for confirmation** in a dialog: the title "Delete X?", the consequence in one sentence, a red button that names the action, and **initial focus on Cancel**. A toast with "Undo" follows. Reversible actions (mark, link, change status) never ask; they only offer "Undo".
6. **Lists are alphabetical by default** (locale-aware, accent-insensitive), including groups, columns and select options. Exceptions: tasks (by urgency) and dated records such as orders (newest first). Use `sortByText`.
7. **Visible progress.** Counters that go down, a day progress bar, a green check for done. Feedback is **subtle**: a 320 ms transition, no confetti.
8. **Save automatically** and show "Saved".
9. **Keyboard first.** `⌘K` for everything, and shortcuts on primary actions.

### Agents (AI features)

For products that put an AI agent in front of customers or money.

1. **Approve before sending.** Anything that goes to a customer or touches money goes through an approval queue. The default is to ask for approval.
2. **Autonomy per task,** never per whole agent. Low-star reviews (1 to 3 stars) always require approval.
3. **Undo, don't confirm.** Sending and discarding show a toast with Undo.
4. **The chat is for the owner,** not for the customer: to test, ask why and adjust. It reads the guidelines and the current data.
5. **Customer-facing replies** are short, factual, make no delivery-time or discount promises, and use no emoji.

### Visual foundations

The authoritative values are the design tokens (see the Tokens page). The summary:

- **Color.** A slightly warm neutral ramp from `#050506` to `#EDEDEA` (text is never pure white). Signals are pastel-bright so they keep contrast on dark: accent `#8AB4FF`, success `#5FD49A`, warning `#E9B65C`, danger `#F07A6E`. Soft backgrounds use `color-mix`.
- **Layers.** canvas, bg, surface, raised, hover. Move one layer at a time; do not skip layers.
- **Type.** Geist (400, 500, 600) for the interface, Geist Mono (400, 500) for data. Display and title use negative tracking.
- **Spacing.** A 4 px grid: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64. Card padding is 20; gaps of 8 to 16 inside components and 24 to 32 between sections.
- **Controls.** Heights 32, 40 (default) and 48. Buttons and inputs share the same height.
- **Radius.** 4 for chips, menu items and checkboxes; 6 for buttons and inputs; 10 for cards, menus and dialogs; pill for badges and switches.
- **Lines.** 1 px always. Subtle for internal dividers, regular for cards, strong for controls and overlays. Dashed means disabled or a total row.
- **Elevation.** Only `--ds-shadow-overlay` and `--ds-shadow-dialog`. No inner shadows, no glow, no blur.
- **States.** Hover is one surface step lighter. There is no press animation. Focus is an accent border plus a 3 px ring. A selected row has a raised background and a 2 px inset ink bar; the active tab has a 2 px ink underline. Disabled controls use reduced opacity and, for inputs, a dashed border.
- **Motion.** Minimal: 150 ms, `cubic-bezier(.2, 0, 0, 1)`, only color, opacity and position. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Backgrounds.** Flat. No gradients, textures or illustrations. Photos appear only in avatars and thumbnails.

### Iconography

- The icon set is **Lucide**, 1.5 px stroke, `currentColor`, **bundled** (never fetched from a CDN at runtime). Import icons from `@loui/ds` (`PlusIcon`, `SearchIcon`, ...), not from `lucide-react`.
- Icons are decorative unless given a label. Icon-only controls use `IconButton`, which requires a `label`.
- No emoji. No filled or colored icons. Unicode glyphs (`+`, `×`, `⌘`) only inside labelled icon buttons.
- Outside the sidebar the system is text-first: actions use a label.

---

## Content guidelines

How the interface talks. These rules apply to every string in the UI: labels, buttons, titles, toasts, errors, empty states and confirmations. They are also available as data in `docs/ai/content-rules.json`.

### Tone

- **Direct, calm, technical without jargon.**
- Speak to "you", usually implied: "Select an order", not "Please select an order".
- State what happened and what to do. Do not blame the user and do not dramatize.

### Casing

- **Sentence case everywhere:** titles, buttons, tabs, menu items. "New order", not "New Order" or "NEW ORDER".
- Uppercase appears only in mono group captions, and it is applied with CSS, never typed.

### Buttons

- **A verb plus an object:** "Create order", "Mark as shipped", "Retry charge".
- Never a bare "OK", "Send" or "Submit".
- Destructive buttons name the action: "Delete order".

### Confirmations

Deleting always asks. The dialog names the object and the consequence in one sentence, the red button names the action, and initial focus is on Cancel.

> **Delete "Northwind Web"?**
> "Northwind Web" and its 14 environments will be removed. This can't be undone.
> [Cancel] [Delete project]

Reversible actions (mark, link, change status) do not ask. They happen and offer "Undo" in a toast.

### Toasts

Short and in the past tense: what just happened.

- "Order #1051 created"
- "3 items archived"

Not "Creating order", not "Success!", not "Order was successfully created".

### Empty states

Say what happened, then what to do.

- "No orders found. Try another filter or search term."

### Errors

Say how to fix the problem.

- "Enter a complete email address."

Not "Invalid email!". Link the message to its field (`aria-describedby`); the `Field` components do this for you.

### Punctuation and symbols

- **No emoji, no exclamation marks, no decorative ellipses.**
- The ellipsis character appears only on menu items that open something that needs more input: "Move to…".
- No "Loading..." or "Saving...". Use a spinner or skeleton, and state the result when it is done.

### Numbers, codes and shortcuts

- Numbers, codes, amounts and shortcuts are set in the mono font (Geist Mono): `ORD-1048`, `$1,240.00`, `⌘K`.
- **Never build currency, dates or numbers by hand.** Format them with `Intl` for the active locale through the provided utilities: `formatCurrency`, `formatDate`, `formatNumber`, `formatPercent`, `formatRelativeDays`.
- Money is an integer in minor units plus an ISO 4217 currency code (ADR-0006). `formatCurrency(124000, 'USD', locale)` renders `$1,240.00`.

### Lists

Alphabetical by default (locale-aware, accent-insensitive), including groups, columns and select options. Use `sortByText`. Exceptions: tasks (by urgency) and dated records (newest first).

### What belongs to the product, not to the design system

Domain vocabulary (for example, an ERP rule that sold units are always called "Quantity") belongs to the product's own guidelines. The design system's built-in strings stay generic.

### Built-in strings and translation

Components contain no user-visible string literals. Every built-in label and ARIA string lives in the component's message catalog (`<Name>.messages.ts`), is written in English following the rules above, and can be overridden per instance or through `DSProvider`. `pt-BR` ships with the library and follows the same tone.

---

## Accessibility

Accessibility is part of the definition of done for every component. The target is **WCAG 2.2 Level AA**, using the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices patterns.

### Conformance target

- Real semantics first: native `<button>`, `<a>`, `<input>`, `<table>` where possible; ARIA only to fill gaps.
- Every interactive element has an accessible name. Icon-only controls require a `label` (enforced by the types).
- Errors, hints and descriptions are programmatically linked (`aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`).
- Visible focus on every focusable element, including in `forced-colors` mode. Focus is never hidden behind sticky UI and is restored when overlays close.
- Contrast: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for UI boundaries and graphics. Every foreground and surface pairing is listed in `tokens.json` with its measured ratio and checked by a unit test.
- Color is never the only carrier of meaning.
- Targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8); default controls are 40 px.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`, `forced-colors` and `prefers-contrast` are respected; 200% text zoom and 320 px reflow are supported.
- Time-limited actions (such as an Undo toast) can be paused by hover or focus and reached by keyboard.

### Keyboard model

React Aria Components provides the behavior; each row becomes contract tests.

| Pattern          | Keys                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Button, link     | `Enter`; button also `Space`                                                                                                                |
| Checkbox, switch | `Space` toggles                                                                                                                             |
| Radio group      | One tab stop (roving); arrow keys move and select, wrapping                                                                                 |
| Tabs             | Roving; `←` `→` move; `Home` `End`; `Tab` moves into the panel                                                                              |
| Menu             | Trigger opens with `Enter`, `Space` or `↓`; `↑` `↓`, `Home` `End`, typeahead; `Enter` or `Space` activates; `Esc` closes and restores focus |
| Combobox         | `↓` `↑` open and move; `Enter` selects; `Esc` closes, then clears                                                                           |
| Dialog, sheet    | Focus trapped; initial focus configurable (Cancel for destructive); `Esc` closes only the top layer; focus returns to trigger               |
| Popover, tooltip | `Esc` closes; tooltips show on focus and hover                                                                                              |
| Tag group        | One tab stop; arrow keys move; `Backspace` or `Delete` removes                                                                              |
| Toast, alert     | Announced through a live region; actions are focusable; auto-dismiss pauses on hover and focus                                              |

Application-level shortcuts use `useHotkey` (for example `Mod+K`); they ignore editable fields and IME composition so they never fight typing.

### How we test

Stories are the single source of states; the tests iterate over them.

| Layer             | Tool                                 | Guards                                                                |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Static            | `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` (strict)    | Role misuse, missing labels                                           |
| Component         | Vitest browser mode (Chromium)       | Props, states, events, controlled and uncontrolled, message overrides |
| Automated a11y    | axe-core through the Storybook addon | Structural WCAG violations on every story; a violation fails the test |
| Keyboard contract | Vitest and story `play` functions    | The keyboard table above                                              |
| Contrast          | Token unit test and browser checks   | Every token pair against its minimum ratio                            |
| Visual            | Screenshot baselines                 | Unintended appearance changes                                         |
| SSR               | Server render tests                  | No `window` access; hydration-safe                                    |
| Manual            | Screen reader checklist per release  | What automation cannot judge                                          |

Rules: a bug fix starts with a failing test; axe rules are never disabled globally; a scoped exception needs a comment with the reason and a task ID.

### Assistive technology

Automated checks cover structure and contrast. Manual screen reader testing (NVDA with Firefox and Chrome, VoiceOver with Safari, TalkBack) is planned per release against a checklist. No manual screen reader pass has been recorded yet, so treat that coverage as not yet performed.

### Known limitations

- Automated tests cannot judge reading order, announcement quality or whether labels make sense; those are reviewed by hand.
- jsdom cannot compute contrast or layout, so contrast and layout checks run in a real browser.
- Dark is the only theme. Contrast has been verified for it and for the `paper` scope; a new theme needs its own verification.

### Reporting an issue

Open an issue with the component, the browser and assistive technology, the steps, and what you expected. Accessibility bugs are treated as defects, not enhancements.

---

## Design tokens

232 tokens; the table lists the 218 semantic and core ones (primitives are listed in tokens.json). Use the CSS variable, never the value.

| CSS variable | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ds-bg-canvas` | `#050506` | Page canvas behind the app shell (the html element). The darkest layer. Not for cards or controls. |
| `--ds-bg` | `#0B0B0C` | Default app background (body, top bar, main area). One step above the canvas. Not for cards; use surface. |
| `--ds-surface` | `#111113` | Cards, panels, table bodies and inputs at rest. Move one layer at a time: bg, surface, surface-raised, surface-hover. |
| `--ds-surface-raised` | `#18181B` | Menus, popovers, selected rows and anything floating above a surface. Not for page backgrounds. |
| `--ds-surface-hover` | `#1F1F23` | Hover state of controls and list items: one step lighter than the resting surface. Do not use at rest. |
| `--ds-surface-row-hover` | `#141416` | Hover background of table and list rows only; subtler than surface-hover so dense data stays calm. Not for buttons or menu items. |
| `--ds-line-subtle` | `#1E1E22` | Internal dividers inside a card or table (row separators). Decorative, so exempt from the 3:1 non-text contrast rule. Never use it as a control boundary. |
| `--ds-line` | `#26262B` | Default 1px border of cards and containers. Not for form control boundaries; use line-control. |
| `--ds-line-strong` | `#33333A` | Border of overlays, menus, popovers, dialogs and cards that must stand out. Not for form control boundaries (use line-control); it is below 3:1. |
| `--ds-line-control` | `#64646B` | Boundary of form controls: input, select, textarea, checkbox, radio and combobox triggers. At least 3:1 on bg, surface and surface-raised (WCAG 1.4.11). New in TOK-004. Not for decorative dividers. |
| `--ds-text` | `#EDEDEA` | Primary text and icons. Warm off-white, not pure white. Use for anything that must be read first. |
| `--ds-text-2` | `#A3A3A9` | Secondary text: descriptions, supporting copy, inactive labels. |
| `--ds-text-3` | `#86868E` | Tertiary text: metadata, placeholders, hints. Meets 4.5:1 on every surface up to surface-hover. Do not use on surfaces lighter than surface-hover or on colored fills. |
| `--ds-text-inverse` | `#0B0B0C` | Text and icons on solid light or signal fills (selected day in a calendar, solid badges). Not on dark surfaces. |
| `--ds-primary-bg` | `#EDEDEA` | Fill of the primary button and the tooltip: light ink on a dark UI. One primary action per screen. Hover is brightness .88, not a new token. |
| `--ds-primary-fg` | `#0B0B0C` | Text and icons on primary-bg. |
| `--ds-primary-fg-muted` | `#5A5A60` | Secondary text on primary-bg (for example the shortcut hint in a tooltip). Only valid on primary-bg. |
| `--ds-accent` | `#8AB4FF` | The single accent: focus, selection, links and open states. Never a button fill or a large area. Always pair with text or a shape, never color alone. |
| `--ds-success` | `#5FD49A` | Success signal: done, saved, healthy. Always accompanied by text or an icon. Not decorative. |
| `--ds-warning` | `#E9B65C` | Warning signal: attention needed, nothing broken. Always accompanied by text or an icon. |
| `--ds-danger` | `#F07A6E` | Error and destructive signal: errors, delete buttons, invalid fields. Always accompanied by text or an icon. |
| `--ds-accent-soft` | `rgba(138, 180, 255, 0.14)` | Tinted background for accent states (selected item, info). 14% accent over the surface beneath, resolved with color-mix so it adapts to the surface. Not for text. |
| `--ds-success-soft` | `rgba(95, 212, 154, 0.14)` | Tinted background for success states (badge, banner). 14% success over the surface beneath. Not for text. |
| `--ds-warning-soft` | `rgba(233, 182, 92, 0.14)` | Tinted background for warning states (badge, banner). 14% warning over the surface beneath. Not for text. |
| `--ds-danger-soft` | `rgba(240, 122, 110, 0.1)` | Tinted background for error states (badge, banner, invalid field). 10% danger over the surface beneath. Not for text. |
| `--ds-danger-soft-hover` | `rgba(240, 122, 110, 0.18)` | Hover state of danger-soft surfaces such as the ghost-danger button. 18% danger over the surface beneath. |
| `--ds-danger-line` | `rgba(240, 122, 110, 0.35)` | Border of danger-tinted surfaces (error banner, destructive confirmation). 35% danger over the surface beneath. Not a form control boundary; invalid fields use danger. |
| `--ds-overlay` | `rgba(5, 5, 6, 0.72)` | Backdrop behind dialogs. Flat, no blur. Not for side sheets; use scrim. |
| `--ds-scrim` | `rgba(5, 5, 6, 0.55)` | Backdrop behind side sheets. Lighter than overlay so the page stays visible. Not for dialogs. |
| `--ds-swatch-ring` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12)` | Inset 1px ring drawn inside color swatches and avatars so dark swatches stay visible on dark surfaces. Not a general border. |
| `--ds-paper` | `#F4F2EC` | Paper surface of printed-document previews (receipt, PDF). The only light surface in the system; use inside [data-theme="paper"] only. |
| `--ds-paper-ink` | `#151515` | Primary text on paper. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-ink-2` | `#3A3A3A` | Secondary text on paper. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-muted` | `#6B6B6B` | Tertiary text and control boundaries on paper (above 4.5:1 on paper). Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-rule` | `#9A968C` | Decorative rules and dividers on paper (table lines, totals). Below 3:1, so never a control boundary or text. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-paper-accent` | `#A95839` | Accent on paper: links and highlighted figures (4.53:1 on paper). Darkened from #B8603E in TOK-004. Paper theme only. |
| `--ds-focus-ring` | `0px 0px 0px 3px rgba(138, 180, 255, 0.25)` | Focus halo: 3px ring, 25% accent over the surface beneath, used as box-shadow next to an accent border. base.css adds a transparent outline so focus stays visible in forced-colors mode. Not a hover or selected style. |
| `--ds-focus-ring-danger` | `0px 0px 0px 3px rgba(240, 122, 110, 0.25)` | Focus halo for invalid fields: 3px ring, 25% danger over the surface beneath. Use instead of focus-ring when the control is in an error state. Not a general error style. |
| `--ds-font-sans` | `Geist, "Geist Fallback", system-ui, sans-serif` | UI font stack: self-hosted Geist, then a metric-matched Arial fallback face, then the system font. Use for all interface text. Not for numbers, codes or data (use font.mono). |
| `--ds-font-mono` | `"Geist Mono", "Geist Mono Fallback", ui-monospace, monospace` | Data font stack: self-hosted Geist Mono with a metric-matched fallback. Use for numbers, codes, amounts, shortcuts and uppercase group captions. Pair with tabular-nums. Not for running text. |
| `--ds-weight-regular` | `400` | Regular weight (400): body text, descriptions, mono data. |
| `--ds-weight-medium` | `500` | Medium weight (500): labels, chips, mono captions. Not for body paragraphs. |
| `--ds-weight-semibold` | `600` | Semibold weight (600): display, title and heading. The heaviest weight in use; do not add bold (700). |
| `--ds-fs-display` | `34px` | Display font size (34px, line 40px, tracking -2%, semibold). Hero statement; at most once per screen. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |
| `--ds-fs-title` | `22px` | Title font size (22px, line 30px, tracking -1%, semibold). Page and section titles. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |
| `--ds-fs-heading` | `17px` | Heading font size (17px, line 24px, semibold). Dialog titles and card headings. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |
| `--ds-fs-body` | `15px` | Body font size (15px, line 24px, regular). Default running text; the base size of the app. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |
| `--ds-fs-small` | `14px` | Small font size (14px, line 22px, regular). Descriptions, helper text and table cells. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |
| `--ds-fs-label` | `13px` | Label font size (13px, line 18px, medium). Field labels, chips and compact buttons. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |
| `--ds-fs-meta` | `12px` | Meta font size (12px, line 16px, mono regular). Dates, phone numbers and counts next to titles. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |
| `--ds-fs-caption` | `11.5px` | Caption font size (11.5px, line 16px, mono medium, uppercase, +8% tracking). FLOOR of the type scale: no token or component may use a smaller size. Group captions and table headers. |
| `--ds-fs-num` | `24px` | Number font size for indicator figures (24px, line 32px, mono medium). Use with tabular-nums. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |
| `--ds-fs-num-lg` | `30px` | Number font size for highlighted totals such as a balance (30px, line 36px, mono medium). Use with tabular-nums. Minimum font size in the system is 11.5px (caption); never go below it. |
| `--ds-fs-icon` | `20px` | Font size of text glyphs inside icon-only buttons (for example the multiplication sign and chevrons), 20px. Not for SVG icons; use size.icon-*. |

| `--ds-tracking-title` | `-0.22px` | Letter spacing for title: -1% of 22px = -0.22px. Use only with fs.title. |

### Pairings that fail contrast

- `--ds-line-control` fails 3:1 on color.surface-hover (2.8:1).

---

## Components

### Alert

> An inline message with a tone, an icon, an optional title, an action and a dismiss button.
The icon is decorative and a visually hidden prefix names the tone for screen readers.

An inline message with a tone, an icon, an optional title, one action and an optional dismiss button.

- Import: `import { Alert } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Alert/Alert.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Alert`): Default, Success, Warning, Danger, Urgent, StaticNotice, TitleOnly, TextOnly, WithAction, Dismissible, LongText, AllTones, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | `'info'` | Kind of message: `info` (neutral, default), `success`, `warning` or `danger`. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Short heading of the alert, in one line: what happened. Plain text, not a document heading. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | The detail: why it happened and what to do. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  |  | A single action next to the text, usually a link or a small `Button` ("Update card"). |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` |  |  | Shows a dismiss button that calls this. The alert is removed by the parent. |
| `urgent` | `boolean` |  | `false` | The message interrupts the user's task and must be announced immediately (`role="alert"`, assertive). Use it only for failures the user must know about right now. |
| `announce` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Whether the alert is a live region (`role="status"`, polite). Default `true`, because most alerts appear after something the user did. Set `false` for a static notice that is part of the page content from the start: it then has no role and is read in page order. Ignored when `urgent`. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ dismiss: string; info: string; success: string; warning: string; danger: string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the built-in messages. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `tone`: `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Alert: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dismiss` | `Dismiss alert` | Name of the dismiss button. |
| `info` | `Information` | Visually hidden prefix that tells screen reader users the kind of alert; color and icon alone cannot. |
| `success` | `Success` |  |
| `warning` | `Warning` |  |
| `danger` | `Error` |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-alert-danger-bg`, `--ds-alert-danger-border`, `--ds-alert-success-bg`, `--ds-alert-success-border`, `--ds-alert-warning-bg`, `--ds-alert-warning-border`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Explain a state that affects the page or a form: a declined payment, a scheduled maintenance, a failed import.
- Tell the user what to do about it, next to the thing it is about.

#### When not to use

- Feedback about an action that just finished ("Order #1051 created"): use `Toast`.
- A confirmation that needs a decision: use `Dialog`.
- A field error: use the field's error message.
- A status of a record (Shipped, Failed): use `Badge`.

#### Anatomy

```
div[role=status | alert | none]  (tinted surface, 1px tinted border, radius lg)
  Icon (decorative)  info | success | warning (triangle) | danger
  content
    VisuallyHidden   "Information" | "Success" | "Warning" | "Error"
    title            optional, 14/22, weight 500
    children         13/18, text-2
  actions            action slot · dismiss IconButton
```

#### Accessibility: role decisions

- **Default `role="status"` (polite).** Most alerts appear after something the user did (submit, import). A status region is announced politely, without stealing focus or interrupting speech. The handoff used `role="alert"` for every `danger` alert, which interrupts for things that are not urgent; urgency is now an explicit `urgent` prop, not a function of the tone.
- **`urgent` gives `role="alert"` (assertive).** Use it for a failure the user must know right now (lost connection, session expired). Avoid more than one at a time.
- **`announce={false}` gives no role.** A notice that is part of the page when it loads (a permanent banner, a form-level note) does not need a live region; screen readers read it in page order. A live region that never changes is noise, and many `status` regions on one page are worse.
- Live regions announce **changes**: for the announcement to work, render the Alert when the event happens and keep the region mounted; do not render it hidden and unhide it.
- **The tone is not only color and icon.** The icon is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden prefix ("Error", "Warning", "Success", "Information", from messages) names the kind of alert for screen readers.
- The **dismiss button** is an `IconButton` named "Dismiss alert" (messages), reachable by Tab and operated with Enter or Space. After dismissing, the parent should move focus somewhere sensible if the alert held it.
- Text contrast on the tinted backgrounds is at least 4.5:1 (checked in the browser test with the real computed colors). The 6% and 30% tints are component tokens (`--ds-alert-*`).
- Forced colors: the browser repaints border and icon with system colors; the icon and the hidden tone prefix still name the tone.

#### Content rules

- Title: what happened, sentence case, no exclamation marks ("Payment declined").
- Text: why and what to do ("The card ending in 4242 was declined. Use another card.").
- The action is a verb plus object ("Update card"), not "Click here".

#### Examples

```tsx
<Alert title="Scheduled maintenance">Sunday, 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" title="Payment declined" action={<Link href="/billing">Update card</Link>}>
  The card ending in 4242 was declined.
</Alert>

<Alert tone="danger" urgent title="Connection lost" onDismiss={() => setOffline(false)}>
  Changes are not being saved.
</Alert>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Badge: A status of a record (Shipped, Failed): use `Badge`.
- Renders: Icon, IconButton, VisuallyHidden

### Avatar

> A circular photo or initials of a person, in grays (never a color per person). The `name`
drives the initials and the accessible name; a photo that fails to load falls back to the
initials.

A circular photo or the initials of a person, in grays. There is no color per person.

- Import: `import { Avatar } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Avatar/Avatar.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Avatar`): Default, Sizes, WithPhoto, BrokenPhoto, Decorative, Shades, Stacked, LongName, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` |  |  | The person's full name. Drives the initials and the accessible name (`alt` of the photo). Optional: still used to compute the initials. |
| `decorative` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Hides the avatar from assistive technology (`alt=""`). Use it when the name is shown next to it. |
| `src` | `string` |  |  | URL of the photo. If it fails to load, the initials are shown instead. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | `sm` 24px, `md` 28px (default), `lg` 40px. |
| `ring` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Draws a 2px ring in the surface color, to separate overlapping avatars. Default `false`. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-avatar-initials-ratio`, `--ds-avatar-ring-width`, `--ds-avatar-size-lg`, `--ds-avatar-size-md`, `--ds-avatar-size-sm`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- Identify who owns, created or is assigned to something.
- Next to a name in a list, a comment or a menu.

#### When not to use

- For a company logo or a product thumbnail: use an image.
- For a status: use `Badge`.

#### Anatomy

```
span.root (circle, role="img" + aria-label when it initials)
  img | span[aria-hidden] initials
```

#### Initials

`getInitials(name, locale)` (also exported) takes the first letter of the first and of the last word: "Ana Maria da Silva" is `AS`; a single word gives one letter. It uses `Intl.Segmenter` (combined characters stay whole) and `toLocaleUpperCase` with the `DSProvider` locale (`i` becomes `İ` in Turkish). The gray shade is derived from the name, so one person always looks the same.

#### Accessibility

- With initials the root is `role="img"` named by `name`; the letters are `aria-hidden` so they are not read twice.
- With a photo the `<img>` has `alt={name}`. A decorative avatar has `alt=""` and no role.
- The handoff set `alt` to the initials ("AL"), which is meaningless to a screen reader; the full name is used now.
- If the image cannot be loaded the initials appear and the accessible name stays the same.
- Avatars are not interactive. Put one inside a button or link that has its own name and mark it `decorative`.

#### Content rules

- Pass the full display name, not the initials.
- Never pass an email or an id as `name`.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" />
<Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" src="/photos/ada.jpg" size="lg" />
<Avatar decorative name="Ada Lovelace" /> <span>Ada Lovelace</span>
```

Stacked avatars: wrap them in a flex container with `role="group"` and an `aria-label`, give each `ring`, and overlap with a negative inline margin. A dedicated `AvatarGroup` is not part of this version.

#### Related components

- Instead, see Badge: For a status: use `Badge`.

### Badge

> A pill with a short status label. The text always states the status; the tone and the
dot only reinforce it.

A pill with a short status label. The text always states the status; the tone and the dot only reinforce it.

- Import: `import { Badge } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Badge/Badge.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Badge`): Default, Accent, Success, Warning, Danger, WithoutDot, AllTones, LongText, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The status text. Required: color and the dot never carry the meaning alone. |
| `tone` | `'neutral' \| 'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | `'neutral'` | Meaning of the badge: `accent` open or in progress, `success` done, `warning` pending, `danger` failed, `neutral` everything else (default). |
| `dot` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Shows the small decorative dot before the text. It is hidden from assistive technology. Default `true`. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `tone`: `neutral`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-accent-soft`, `--ds-badge-dot-size`, `--ds-badge-height`, `--ds-badge-padding-inline`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-danger-soft`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-success-soft`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-warning`, `--ds-warning-soft`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Show the state of a record in a list, a table row or a card header: Draft, In progress, Shipped, Failed.
- Keep the text short (one to three words, sentence case).

#### When not to use

- For a count or a filter value: use `Tag`.
- For a message the user must read or act on: use `Alert`.
- For an action: use `Button`. A Badge is never interactive.

#### Anatomy

```
[ dot ] Text
```

- `dot` (optional, decorative, `aria-hidden`).
- `text`: required, the status.

#### Accessibility

- A Badge is plain text in a `span`: there is no role and no keyboard behavior.
- The dot is `aria-hidden`; the tone is never the only carrier of meaning, because the text names the status (WCAG 1.4.1).
- Text on every soft tint keeps at least 4.5:1 contrast (checked in the browser test by compositing the real computed colors).
- In forced-colors mode the Badge gets a border and the dot takes the text color.

#### Content rules

- Sentence case, no punctuation, no emoji: "In progress", not "IN PROGRESS!".
- Name the state, not the action: "Shipped", not "Ship".
- If the status can be unknown, say so with text ("Unknown"), do not omit the Badge.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Shipped</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger">Failed</Badge>
<Badge dot={false}>Draft</Badge>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Tag: For a count or a filter value: use `Tag`.
- Instead, see Alert: For a message the user must read or act on: use `Alert`.
- Instead, see Button: For an action: use `Button`. A Badge is never interactive.

### Button

> An action button built on React Aria's `Button`.

Use one `primary` button per screen. While `isPending` the button keeps its width, shows a
spinner, stays focusable, sets `aria-disabled` and ignores presses, so it can be explained
by a tooltip and focus is never lost.

The control for an action. Built on React Aria's `Button`, styled with tokens and `data-*` state attributes.

- Handoff source: `components/forms/Button` (CMP-FRM-01).

- Import: `import { Button } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Button/Button.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Button`): Default, Primary, Secondary, Ghost, Danger, DangerSolid, Variants, Sizes, WithLeadingIcon, WithTrailingShortcut, FullWidth, Disabled, Pending, PendingVariants, LongText, Rtl, KeyboardActivation, Focused, Hovered

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger' \| 'danger-solid'` |  | `'secondary'` | Visual style. - `primary`: the single main action of the screen (light ink on dark). One per screen. - `secondary`: default for other actions. - `ghost`: tertiary, low emphasis actions. - `danger`: destructive action that is not yet confirmed. - `danger-solid`: the confirm button of a destructive dialog. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | Height token: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Stretch to the width of the container. |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Node before the label, usually `<Icon size="sm" />`. Decorative; the label names the button. |
| `trailing` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Node after the label, for example a `Kbd` shortcut hint. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Label: a short verb plus object in sentence case ("Create order"). |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` |  |  | Ref to the underlying `<button>` element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaBaseButtonProps` (react-aria): `aria-controls`, `aria-current`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-pressed`, `form`, `formAction`, `formEncType`, `formMethod`, `formNoValidate`, `formTarget`, `name`, `preventFocusOnPress`, `type`, `value`
- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`
- From `ButtonProps` (react-aria): `isDisabled`
- From `ButtonProps` (react-aria-components): `isPending`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusableDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `excludeFromTabOrder`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `HoverEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onHoverChange`, `onHoverEnd`, `onHoverStart`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `variant`: `primary`, `secondary`, `ghost`, `danger`, `danger-solid`
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-button-danger-solid-hover-brightness`, `--ds-button-hover-brightness`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-danger-line`, `--ds-danger-soft`, `--ds-danger-soft-hover`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-body`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-body`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-primary-bg`, `--ds-primary-fg`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-4`, `--ds-space-5`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-inverse`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### One primary per screen

Use **one `primary` button per screen**, at the top right of the view, ideally with a keyboard shortcut. Primary is "ink for action": light on dark, never the accent color. Every other action is `secondary` or `ghost`. A second primary button means the screen has two main jobs: split the screen or demote one action.

#### When to use

- To run an action in place: "Create order", "Mark as shipped".
- `danger` for a destructive action that opens a confirmation, `danger-solid` for the confirm button inside that dialog (initial focus stays on Cancel).
- `ghost` for low-emphasis actions such as "View all" in a card header.

#### When not to use

- To navigate to another page: use `Link` (styled as text) so the browser keeps link semantics.
- For an icon-only action: use `IconButton`, which requires an accessible name.
- For a two-state toggle: use a toggle component.

#### Anatomy

`[leading] label [trailing]` inside one native `<button>`. When pending, the content keeps its box (invisible) and a `Spinner` is centered on top, so the width never changes.

#### Accessibility

- A real `<button>`; the name is its visible label.
- Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` and `Space` press (RAC). One tab stop.
- Focus: accent border plus a 3px ring through `data-focus-visible`, a transparent outline that forced-colors mode repaints as `Highlight`. Mouse clicks do not show the ring.
- Pending: the button stays in the tab order (focus is not lost while waiting) with `aria-disabled="true"` (React Aria does not set `aria-busy`). React Aria announces the busy state when the focused button becomes pending and again when it finishes. The spinner is named "Loading" (pt-BR "Carregando", from the `Spinner` messages) and sits inside the button so it is part of the button's content.
- Disabled: removed from the tab order. Explain _why_ in nearby text rather than relying on a disabled button alone.
- Targets: at least 32px high, above the 24px minimum of WCAG 2.5.8.
- Contrast: label colors meet 4.5:1 on their backgrounds in every variant; disabled controls are exempt.
- Reduced motion: the only transition is a 150ms background color change, which the global reduced-motion rule neutralizes. The pending spinner turns into a static ring.

#### Content rules

- Verb plus object, sentence case: "Create order", "Retry charge". Never a bare "OK" or "Send".
- Destructive buttons name the action: "Delete order".
- No exclamation marks, no emoji, no decorative ellipsis. Use "..." only when the action opens something that needs more input ("Move to...").

#### States

Hover (one surface step lighter; primary dims with `--ds-button-hover-brightness`), focus-visible, disabled, pending. Hover, focus and pending are CSS (`data-hovered`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-pending`), never React state. There is no press animation.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" onPress={save}>Save changes</Button>

<Button leading={<Icon icon={PlusIcon} size="sm" />}>Create order</Button>

<Button variant="primary" isPending={isSaving} onPress={save}>
  Save changes
</Button>

<Button trailing={<span className="ds-mono">⌘K</span>}>Search</Button>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Link: To navigate to another page: use `Link` (styled as text) so the browser keeps link semantics.
- Instead, see IconButton: For an icon-only action: use `IconButton`, which requires an accessible name.
- Renders: Spinner

### Card

> A bordered surface that groups related content. With a `title` it is a labelled region
(`section` named by its heading).

A bordered surface that groups related content. With a `title` it is a labelled region.

- Import: `import { Card } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Card/Card.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Card`): Default, WithActions, Raised, WithoutTitle, HeadingLevel3, NoPadding, LongText, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Title shown as an uppercase mono caption. It is a real heading (see `headingLevel`) and names the card region through `aria-labelledby`. |
| `headingLevel` | `'1' \| '2' \| '3' \| '4' \| '5' \| '6'` |  | `'2'` | Heading level of the title (`h1` to `h6`). Pick the level that fits the page outline. Default `2`. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Controls placed at the end of the header, next to the title (buttons, a menu). |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'raised'` |  | `'default'` | `default` is a flat surface with a border. `raised` uses the raised surface, a stronger border and the overlay shadow: use it only for a card that floats above the page (a pinned panel, a detail popover shell), never for cards that sit in the normal flow. |
| `padding` | `'md' \| 'none'` |  | `'md'` | `md` applies the card padding token; `none` removes it (for full-bleed content such as a table). Default `md`. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `variant`: `default`, `raised`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-card-gap`, `--ds-card-padding`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-line`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-tracking-caption`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Group a set of related fields, numbers or a list under one caption.
- Put page sections side by side in a grid.

#### When not to use

- To wrap a whole page: use the page layout.
- For content that interrupts the user: use `Dialog` or `Alert`.
- Do not nest a Card inside a Card; use a divider instead.

#### Anatomy

```
section (surface + 1px line, radius lg, padding)
  header (optional)
    h{headingLevel}  mono caption, uppercase by CSS
    actions          optional controls
  children
```

#### Elevation

Borders carry hierarchy, shadows are for overlays (AGENTS.md section 5). A `raised` card gets the raised surface, a stronger border **and** `--ds-shadow-overlay`, so use it only when the card really floats (a pinned side panel, the shell of a custom popover). A card in the normal flow stays `default`.

#### Accessibility

- The root is a `section`. With a `title`, the heading id is wired to `aria-labelledby`, so screen readers expose a named `region` landmark. Without a title or a label it is a plain generic container (no landmark), which is correct for decorative grouping.
- Give a title-less card an `aria-label` when it should be a landmark.
- The heading level is yours to choose: keep levels sequential (a Card inside a page with an `h1` usually uses `2`; inside another section use `3`).
- The caption uses `--ds-text-2` (the handoff used `--ds-text-3`, which drops below 4.5:1 on the raised surface).

#### Content rules

- Captions are sentence case in the source ("Storage"); uppercase is applied by CSS only.
- Keep captions to one to three words.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Card title="Storage" actions={<Button size="sm">Manage</Button>}>
  <Progress value={62} label="Used" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" />
</Card>

<Card title="Details" headingLevel={3}>…</Card>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Alert: For content that interrupts the user: use `Dialog` or `Alert`.

### Checkbox

> A checkbox with a native `<input type="checkbox">` (so `name` / `value` take part in form
submission), an 18px box and an optional description. The whole label row is the click target.

State props follow React Aria: `isSelected`, `defaultSelected` and `onChange(isSelected)`.
`isIndeterminate` is visual and semantic ("mixed") until the user toggles it.

A checkbox with a native `<input type="checkbox">`, an 18px box and an optional description, plus a labelled group for several related checkboxes. Built on React Aria `CheckboxField` + `CheckboxButton` (the non-deprecated pair that supports a description and an error outside the label) and `CheckboxGroup`. Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md).

- Import: `import { Checkbox } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Checkbox/Checkbox.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Checkbox`): Default, Checked, Indeterminate, WithDescription, Required, Invalid, Disabled, ReadOnly, LongLabel, WithoutVisibleLabel, InAGroup, GroupHorizontal, GroupInvalid

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Secondary text under the label. Linked with `aria-describedby`, not part of the name. |
| `errorMessage` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  | Error text, for example "Accept the terms to continue". Shown while the checkbox is invalid and the error is displayed (after a submit attempt with the default native validation). Inside a `CheckboxGroup` put the error on the group instead. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the field root. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ requiredMark: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`). |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the field root `<div>`. Use `inputRef` for the `<input>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `AriaToggleProps` (react-aria): `aria-controls`
- From `AriaValidationProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-errormessage`
- From `CheckboxFieldProps` (react-aria-components): `inputRef`
- From `CheckboxProps` (react-aria): `isIndeterminate`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusableDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `excludeFromTabOrder`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `InputBase` (@react-types/shared): `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`
- From `InputDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `form`, `name`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `RACValidation` (react-aria-components): `validationBehavior`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- From `ToggleProps` (react-stately): `value`
- From `ToggleStateOptions` (react-stately): `defaultSelected`, `isSelected`, `onChange`
- From `Validation` (@react-types/shared): `isInvalid`, `isRequired`, `validate`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-checkbox-box-size`, `--ds-checkbox-radius`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-choice-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-5`, `--ds-target-min`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-text-inverse`

#### When to use

- Independent yes/no choices, agreement ("I accept the terms"), selecting rows, picking several items from a list (`CheckboxGroup`).
- `isIndeterminate` for a parent that summarizes partly selected children.

#### When not to use

- An on/off setting that applies at once: `Switch`.
- One choice from several: `RadioGroup`.

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop                                                      | Notes                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`                                                   | Visible label. Without it pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (type error otherwise).         |
| `description`                                             | Secondary text under the label, linked by `aria-describedby`, not part of the name.              |
| `errorMessage`                                            | Error for a single checkbox (for example a required agreement). In a group, set it on the group. |
| `isSelected` / `defaultSelected` / `onChange(isSelected)` | React Aria naming for controlled and uncontrolled use.                                           |
| `isIndeterminate`                                         | Shows a minus; the native input is `indeterminate` until toggled.                                |
| `name`, `value`                                           | Submitted with the form while checked (`value` defaults to `on`).                                |
| `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`     | Standard states.                                                                                 |
| `inputRef` / `ref`                                        | `inputRef` is the `<input>`, `ref` the field root.                                               |

`CheckboxGroup` takes `label`, `description`, `errorMessage`, `orientation` (`vertical` default, `horizontal`), `name`, `value`/`defaultValue`/`onChange(values: string[])`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`. Each child `Checkbox` needs a `value`.

#### Look

- 18px box, radius from `--ds-checkbox-radius` (5px), `--ds-line-control` border (3:1 or better in every state), accent fill with a `--ds-text-inverse` check when selected, minus when indeterminate.
- Hover brightens the border; it never changes the fill.
- The whole row is the click target and is at least 24px tall (WCAG 2.5.8).
- A disabled group dims once as a whole; disabled single checkboxes use `--ds-opacity-disabled`.

#### Accessibility

- Space toggles the focused checkbox. Tab moves between checkboxes; each checkbox is a tab stop.
- Name comes from the label only; the description is `aria-describedby`.
- Group: `role="group"` named by the label, with the group description and error.
- Forced colors: borders and the check glyph use system colors; the glyph (check or minus) carries the state.

#### Example

```tsx
<Checkbox label="I accept the terms" name="terms" isRequired errorMessage="Accept the terms to continue." />

<CheckboxGroup label="Notify me about" name="topics" defaultValue={['orders']}>
  <Checkbox value="orders" label="New orders" />
  <Checkbox value="stock" label="Low stock" description="When a fabric drops below its minimum." />
</CheckboxGroup>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Switch: An on/off setting that applies at once: `Switch`.
- Instead, see RadioGroup: One choice from several: `RadioGroup`.
- Renders: FieldMessages, Icon, RequiredMark

### CheckboxGroup

> A labelled `role="group"` of checkboxes that share one value (`string[]`), one `name`, and
one description and error. `value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange(values)` follow React Aria.

A checkbox with a native `<input type="checkbox">`, an 18px box and an optional description, plus a labelled group for several related checkboxes. Built on React Aria `CheckboxField` + `CheckboxButton` (the non-deprecated pair that supports a description and an error outside the label) and `CheckboxGroup`. Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md).

- Import: `import { CheckboxGroup } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Checkbox/CheckboxGroup.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Checkbox`): Default, Checked, Indeterminate, WithDescription, Required, Invalid, Disabled, ReadOnly, LongLabel, WithoutVisibleLabel, InAGroup, GroupHorizontal, GroupInvalid

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The `Checkbox` elements of the group. Each needs a `value`. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Helper text under the label. Linked with `aria-describedby`. |
| `errorMessage` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  | Error text for the group, shown while it is invalid and the error is displayed. |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` |  | `'vertical'` | Layout of the checkboxes. Default `vertical`. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the group root. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ requiredMark: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`). |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the group root `<div>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `AriaValidationProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-errormessage`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `InputBase` (@react-types/shared): `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`
- From `InputDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `form`, `name`
- From `RACValidation` (react-aria-components): `validationBehavior`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- From `Validation` (@react-types/shared): `isInvalid`, `isRequired`, `validate`
- From `ValueBase` (@react-types/shared): `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `value`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-checkbox-box-size`, `--ds-checkbox-radius`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-choice-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-5`, `--ds-target-min`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-text-inverse`

#### When to use

- Independent yes/no choices, agreement ("I accept the terms"), selecting rows, picking several items from a list (`CheckboxGroup`).
- `isIndeterminate` for a parent that summarizes partly selected children.

#### When not to use

- An on/off setting that applies at once: `Switch`.
- One choice from several: `RadioGroup`.

#### Props (key ones)

| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| `name`, `value`                                           | Submitted with the form while checked (`value` defaults to `on`).                                |
| `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`     | Standard states.                                                                                 |
| `inputRef` / `ref`                                        | `inputRef` is the `<input>`, `ref` the field root.                                               |

`CheckboxGroup` takes `label`, `description`, `errorMessage`, `orientation` (`vertical` default, `horizontal`), `name`, `value`/`defaultValue`/`onChange(values: string[])`, `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`. Each child `Checkbox` needs a `value`.

- 18px box, radius from `--ds-checkbox-radius` (5px), `--ds-line-control` border (3:1 or better in every state), accent fill with a `--ds-text-inverse` check when selected, minus when indeterminate.
- Hover brightens the border; it never changes the fill.
- The whole row is the click target and is at least 24px tall (WCAG 2.5.8).
- A disabled group dims once as a whole; disabled single checkboxes use `--ds-opacity-disabled`.

- Space toggles the focused checkbox. Tab moves between checkboxes; each checkbox is a tab stop.
- Name comes from the label only; the description is `aria-describedby`.
- Group: `role="group"` named by the label, with the group description and error.
- Forced colors: borders and the check glyph use system colors; the glyph (check or minus) carries the state.

```tsx
<Checkbox label="I accept the terms" name="terms" isRequired errorMessage="Accept the terms to continue." />

<CheckboxGroup label="Notify me about" name="topics" defaultValue={['orders']}>
  <Checkbox value="orders" label="New orders" />
  <Checkbox value="stock" label="Low stock" description="When a fabric drops below its minimum." />
```
