### Description

> Helper text under a field (the handoff `hint`). Linked to the control with
`aria-describedby` by the surrounding React Aria field. It stays visible when an error shows.

Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

- Import: `import { Description } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Field/Field.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Field`): Anatomy, ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt, RealtimeValidation

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### Exports

| Export                                 | What it is                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Label`                                | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker.                                                         |
| `Description`                          | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`.                                                     |
| `FieldError`                           | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. |
| `FieldMessages`                        | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box.                                                                                  |
| `RequiredMark`                         | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`.                                                                                                       |
| `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel`      | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel<P>` helps type stories.                                       |
| `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result).                                                                               |

#### Anatomy and spacing

```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

#### One state model (ARCH-009)

| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

#### Required marker

`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

#### Validation behavior: native (default), and why

React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language.
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

#### Accessibility

- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

#### Related components

- Used by: Radio, RadioGroup

### EmptyState

> Tells the user that there is nothing to show, why, and what to do next. The copy follows
"what happened + what to do".

A typographic placeholder for a list, table or panel that has nothing to show. It says what happened and what the user can do about it.

- Import: `import { EmptyState } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/EmptyState/EmptyState.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/EmptyState`): Default, WithActions, Compact, WithoutBorder, WithIcon, TitleOnly, LongText, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | What happened, in one short sentence: "No orders found". Rendered as a heading (see `headingLevel`). |
| `headingLevel` | `'1' \| '2' \| '3' \| '4' \| '5' \| '6'` |  | `'2'` | Heading level of the title (`h1` to `h6`). Pick the level that fits the page outline. Default `2`. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | What the user can do about it: "Try another filter or search term." |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Optional icon above the title. Decorative: it is hidden from assistive technology. No illustrations. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  |  | The primary action, usually a `Button`. Rendered after the secondary action. |
| `secondaryAction` | `ReactNode` |  |  | A second, lower-emphasis action. |
| `compact` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Less padding and a smaller title, for use inside a card, a panel or a table. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` |  | `true` | Dashed border. Set to `false` when the empty state already sits inside a bordered container. Default `true`. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-empty-state-compact-padding-block`, `--ds-empty-state-compact-padding-inline`, `--ds-empty-state-description-max-w`, `--ds-empty-state-padding-block`, `--ds-empty-state-padding-inline`, `--ds-fs-heading`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-heading`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-radius-lg`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-semibold`

#### When to use

- A list, table or search has no results.
- A feature has no data yet and the user can create some.

#### When not to use

- While data is loading: use `Skeleton`.
- When loading failed: use `Alert` with a retry action.
- For a short inline note inside a field: use the field's description.

#### Anatomy

```
div.root (dashed border, centered)
  span[aria-hidden]  icon (optional)
  h{headingLevel}    title
  p                  description (optional)
  div                secondaryAction, action
```

#### Copy: what happened + what to do

Title: say what is missing, in sentence case, without apologies or exclamation marks. Description: tell the user the next step, in one sentence.

| Situation        | Title             | Description                                              | Action        |
| ---------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Filtered to zero | No orders found   | Try another filter or search term.                       | Clear filters |
| First use        | No orders yet     | Orders created here or in the store appear in this list. | Create order  |
| Cleared inbox    | Nothing to review | New approvals appear here as they arrive.                | (none)        |

Avoid "Oops", "Sorry", blame ("You have no orders") and filler ("There is nothing to show here at the moment").

#### Accessibility

- The title is a real heading: choose `headingLevel` so the outline stays sequential. The heading lets screen reader users find the empty region by navigating headings.
- The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the text carries the meaning.
- The component does not announce itself. If the empty state replaces content after a user action (for example a search), announce the result count in your own live region.
- Actions are ordinary buttons or links with their own names; order in the DOM is secondary then primary, matching the visual order.

#### Examples

```tsx
<EmptyState
  title="No orders found"
  description="Try another filter or search term."
  action={<Button>Clear filters</Button>}
/>

<EmptyState compact bordered={false} headingLevel={3} title="No comments" />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Skeleton: While data is loading: use `Skeleton`.
- Instead, see Alert: When loading failed: use `Alert` with a retry action.

### FieldError

> Error text of a field. Renders only while the field is invalid and the error is *displayed*:
with the default `validationBehavior="native"` that is after a submit attempt (see Field.md).
The message sits in a `role="alert"` element so it is announced when it appears; on submit focus also
moves to the first invalid field, which reads it again through `aria-describedby`.

Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

- Import: `import { FieldError } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Field/Field.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Field`): Anatomy, ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt, RealtimeValidation

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  | The message. A function receives the validation result. Without children, RAC shows the validation errors (the browser's message for native constraints). |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  |  |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### Exports

| Export                                 | What it is                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Label`                                | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker.                                                         |
| `Description`                          | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`.                                                     |
| `FieldError`                           | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. |
| `FieldMessages`                        | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box.                                                                                  |
| `RequiredMark`                         | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`.                                                                                                       |
| `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel`      | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel<P>` helps type stories.                                       |
| `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result).                                                                               |

#### Anatomy and spacing

```

  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

### FieldMessages

> Description followed by the error: the footer every field renders under its control.

Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

- Import: `import { FieldMessages } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Field/Field.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Field`): Anatomy, ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt, RealtimeValidation

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |  |
| `errorMessage` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### Exports

| Export                                 | What it is                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Label`                                | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker.                                                         |
| `Description`                          | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`.                                                     |
| `FieldError`                           | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. |
| `FieldMessages`                        | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box.                                                                                  |
| `RequiredMark`                         | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`.                                                                                                       |
| `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel`      | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel<P>` helps type stories.                                       |
| `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result).                                                                               |

#### Anatomy and spacing

```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

#### One state model (ARCH-009)

| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

#### Required marker

`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

#### Validation behavior: native (default), and why

React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language.
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

#### Accessibility

- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

#### Related components

- Used by: Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, Input, Radio, RadioGroup, Select, Switch, Textarea

### Icon

> An inline SVG icon (Lucide, bundled) that inherits the text color and draws a 1.5px stroke.
Decorative by default; pass `label` to make it a meaningful image.

An inline SVG icon from the curated Lucide set. It inherits the text color, draws a 1.5px stroke and is hidden from assistive technology unless you give it a `label`.

- Replaces: the runtime `unpkg.com/lucide-static` CSS-mask loading (ICON-001), text glyphs used as icons (ICON-002) and the ad hoc icon rules (ICON-003).
- Built on: `lucide-react`, bundled and tree-shakeable. No network access, no CDN.

- Import: `import { Icon } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Icon/Icon.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Icon`): Default, Sizes, WithLabel, InheritsColor, DirectionalRtl, Gallery

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `LucideIcon` | yes |  | The icon to draw, one of the curated set exported from this package (for example `SearchIcon`). |
| `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | Size token: `xs` 12px, `sm` 14px, `md` 18px (default), `lg` 20px. |
| `label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name. Omit it when the icon only decorates text that already names the control (the icon is then hidden from assistive technology). Set it only when the icon carries meaning on its own, outside a control that has its own name. |
| `directional` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Mirror the icon horizontally in right-to-left languages. Set it for icons that point in a reading direction (chevrons, arrows); leave it off for symmetric or universal icons. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-icon-lg`, `--ds-icon-md`, `--ds-icon-sm`, `--ds-icon-stroke-width`, `--ds-icon-xs`

#### When to use

- Next to a text label to reinforce it (button leading slot, menu item, alert, input affordance).
- Inside `IconButton`, which supplies the accessible name.
- On its own only when it carries meaning that no nearby text states. Then set `label`.

#### When not to use

- As the only carrier of meaning or status. Color and shape never replace text.
- For filled, colored or multi-color icons, emoji or Unicode glyphs. Use the set below.
- For a loading indicator that moves: use `Spinner`.
- For an icon that is not in the set. Add it to `icons.ts` with a documented use first.

#### Anatomy

A single `<svg>` (24x24 viewBox) with a `currentColor` stroke and no fill. Size and stroke come from tokens: `--ds-icon-xs|sm|md|lg` and `--ds-icon-stroke-width`.

#### The curated set

Import icons from the package, not from `lucide-react`: `import { Icon, SearchIcon } from '@loui/ds'`.

`iconSet` maps the kebab-case names below to the components and `iconNames` documents the use of each. Both are the source of the allow-list in the manifest (AI-002).

arrow-down, arrow-left, arrow-right, arrow-up, calendar, check, chevron-down, chevron-left, chevron-right, chevron-up, chevrons-up-down, circle-alert, circle-check, circle-x, ellipsis, external-link, info, loader, minus, plus, search, star, triangle-alert, x.

#### Accessibility

- Decorative by default: `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`.
- With `label`: `role="img"` and `aria-label`. Use short, specific names ("Saved", not "check icon").
- An icon inside a control never names the control. Put the name on the control (`IconButton label`).
- Forced colors: the stroke is `currentColor`, so it follows the system text color.
- Contrast: icons that convey meaning need 3:1 against their background (WCAG 1.4.11).
- Reduced motion: icons do not animate.

#### Content rules

- Labels are sentence case and describe the meaning ("Saved"), never the picture ("Green check").
- No emoji or text glyphs as icons (AGENTS.md section 7).

#### Examples

```tsx
import { Button, CircleCheckIcon, ChevronRightIcon, Icon, PlusIcon } from '@loui/ds';

<Button leading={<Icon icon={PlusIcon} size="sm" />}>Create order</Button>;

<Icon icon={CircleCheckIcon} label="Paid" />;

<Icon icon={ChevronRightIcon} directional />;
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Spinner: For a loading indicator that moves: use `Spinner`.
- Used by: Alert, Checkbox, IconButton, Link, Select, Tag, TagGroup

### IconButton

> A square button with a single icon and a required accessible name.

The `label` becomes `aria-label`; there is no `title` (it would duplicate the name and is
not keyboard accessible). A tooltip that shows the label on hover and focus is a separate,
later addition.

A square button that holds one icon and has a required accessible name. Built on React Aria's `Button`.

- Handoff source: `components/forms/IconButton` (CMP-FRM-02).

- Import: `import { IconButton } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/IconButton/IconButton.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/IconButton`): Default, Ghost, Variants, Sizes, Disabled, Toolbar, AccessibleName, KeyboardActivation, Focused, Hovered

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | Accessible name, required. Say what the button does, as a verb plus object when there is one ("Add order", "Close dialog"), not what it looks like ("Plus"). |
| `icon` | `LucideIcon` | yes |  | The icon to draw: one of the curated set (for example `PlusIcon`). Decorative inside the button. |
| `variant` | `'secondary' \| 'ghost'` |  | `'secondary'` | Visual style: `secondary` (default, bordered) or `ghost` (no border at rest). |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | Square size token: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` |  |  | Ref to the underlying `<button>` element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaBaseButtonProps` (react-aria): `aria-controls`, `aria-current`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-pressed`, `form`, `formAction`, `formEncType`, `formMethod`, `formNoValidate`, `formTarget`, `name`, `preventFocusOnPress`, `type`, `value`
- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `ButtonProps` (react-aria): `isDisabled`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusableDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `excludeFromTabOrder`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `HoverEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onHoverChange`, `onHoverEnd`, `onHoverStart`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `variant`: `secondary`, `ghost`
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-target-min`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`

#### When to use

- A compact action whose meaning is clear from context and icon: close, add, more actions, search.
- Toolbars and card headers where a text button would not fit.

#### When not to use

- When there is room for a text label: use `Button` with a `leading` icon. A visible word is clearer than any icon.
- For navigation: use `Link`.
- For an action whose icon is ambiguous: write the label out in a `Button`.

#### Anatomy

One native `<button>` containing a decorative `Icon`. No visible text, no `title`.

#### Accessibility

- `label` is required by the type (`label: string`), which enforces AGENTS.md section 8.
- The name is `aria-label` only. The handoff set `title` too, which duplicated the name and was not available to keyboard or touch users. A tooltip (shown on hover **and** focus, dismissible with `Esc`) will be added with the `Tooltip` component; until then use a clear `label`.
- The icon is `aria-hidden` and `focusable="false"`; the button is never named by its glyph.
- Target size: 32 / 40 / 48 px, above the 24px minimum of WCAG 2.5.8 (`--ds-target-min` is also enforced as `min-inline-size` and `min-block-size`).
- Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` and `Space` press.
- Focus: accent border plus 3px ring on keyboard focus; forced-colors mode repaints the transparent outline.
- Contrast: the icon uses `--ds-text` (secondary) or `--ds-text-2` (ghost) on the surface, both above 4.5:1 and well above the 3:1 needed for graphics.
- Reduced motion: only a 150ms background transition, neutralized by the global rule.

#### Content rules

- `label`: verb plus object in sentence case, without the word "button" or "icon": "Add order", "Close dialog", "More actions".
- Translate it like any other text; `IconButton` has no built-in strings.

#### Examples

```tsx
<IconButton label="Add order" icon={PlusIcon} onPress={addOrder} />

<IconButton variant="ghost" size="sm" label="More actions" icon={EllipsisIcon} />

<div role="toolbar" aria-label="Order actions">
  <IconButton variant="ghost" label="Search orders" icon={SearchIcon} />
  <IconButton variant="ghost" label="Close panel" icon={XIcon} />
</div>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Button: When there is room for a text label: use `Button` with a `leading` icon. A visible word is clearer than any icon.
- Instead, see Link: For navigation: use `Link`.
- Renders: Icon
- Used by: Alert

### Input

> Single-line text field: label, control, description and error wired together
(`for`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`), built on React Aria `TextField`.

Consumer `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onKeyDown` etc. are composed with the internal handlers, so
they never break the focus ring (a defect of the handoff).

Single-line text field with a label, helper text and error text wired together. Built on React Aria `TextField` + `Input`; see [Field](../Field/Field.md) for the shared states, spacing and validation timing.

- Import: `import { Input } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Input/Input.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Input`): Default, WithDescription, Required, Invalid, Disabled, ReadOnly, Mono, Sizes, WithAdornments, LongLabel, Focused, FocusKeepsRingWithConsumerHandlers

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Helper text under the control (handoff `hint`). Linked with `aria-describedby`. |
| `errorMessage` | `FieldErrorMessage` |  |  | Error text (handoff `error`). Shown while the field is invalid *and* the error is displayed: after a submit attempt with the default `validationBehavior="native"`, or at once when you control `isInvalid`. A function receives the validation result. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  | Text shown while the field is empty. Never a substitute for the label. |
| `mono` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Geist Mono with tabular figures, for codes, identifiers and numbers. |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Decoration before the text, usually an `Icon`. Keep it decorative or give it its own name. |
| `trailing` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Content after the text: a unit, a shortcut hint (`Kbd`), or an `IconButton`. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` |  | `'md'` | Control height: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the field root (label, control and messages). |
| `inputClassName` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the `<input>` element. |
| `inputRef` | `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` |  |  | Ref to the `<input>` element. The `ref` prop points at the field root. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ requiredMark: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`). |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the field root `<div>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `AriaTextFieldProps` (react-aria): `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-autocomplete`, `aria-controls`, `aria-haspopup`, `enterKeyHint`
- From `AriaValidationProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-errormessage`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusableDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `excludeFromTabOrder`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `InputBase` (@react-types/shared): `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`
- From `InputDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `form`, `name`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `RACValidation` (react-aria-components): `validationBehavior`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- From `TextFieldProps` (react-aria-components): `isInvalid`
- From `TextInputDOMEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBeforeInput`, `onCompositionEnd`, `onCompositionStart`, `onCompositionUpdate`, `onCopy`, `onCut`, `onInput`, `onPaste`, `onSelect`
- From `TextInputDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoComplete`, `autoCorrect`, `inputMode`, `maxLength`, `minLength`, `pattern`, `spellCheck`, `type`
- From `Validation` (@react-types/shared): `isRequired`, `validate`
- From `ValueBase` (@react-types/shared): `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `value`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-field-control-padding-inline`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-text-3`

#### When to use

- Short free text, codes, emails, search terms, numbers typed as text.
- Use `mono` for codes and identifiers (`ORD-1048`).

#### When not to use

- Several lines of text: `Textarea`.
- A choice from a list: `Select`, `RadioGroup`, `Checkbox`.
- Currency or quantity entry that needs masking: a dedicated field (`CurrencyInput`, planned).

#### Anatomy

```
Label *                          required marker (aria-hidden)
[ leading  value / placeholder  trailing ]
Description
Error
```

#### Props (key ones)

| Prop                                                                | Notes                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                                                             | Visible label. Without it you must pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (type error otherwise). |
| `description`                                                       | Helper text (handoff `hint`).                                                                     |
| `errorMessage`                                                      | Error text (handoff `error`), node or function of the validation result. Needs an invalid state.  |
| `isInvalid` / `isRequired` / `isReadOnly` / `isDisabled`            | Standard states. `isInvalid` shows the error at once.                                             |
| `size`                                                              | `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px.                                                        |
| `mono`                                                              | Geist Mono with tabular figures.                                                                  |
| `leading` / `trailing`                                              | Adornments inside the box: an `Icon`, a unit, a `Kbd` hint, an `IconButton`.                      |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`                        | Controlled and uncontrolled, React Aria naming (`onChange` receives the string, not the event).   |
| `name`, `type`, `autoComplete`, `inputMode`, `maxLength`, `pattern` | Passed to the `<input>`; `name` and the value take part in form submission.                       |
| `validate`, `validationBehavior`                                    | See Field.md.                                                                                     |
| `inputRef` / `ref`                                                  | `inputRef` is the `<input>`, `ref` the field root.                                                |
| `messages`                                                          | `requiredMark` override.                                                                          |

All other props of React Aria `TextField` are accepted (`onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onKeyDown`, `autoFocus`, `form`, ...). They are composed with the internal handlers, never replacing them.

#### Accessibility

- Native `<input>` named by `<label for>`; description and error are in `aria-describedby`; `aria-invalid` when invalid; `required` when required.
- Keyboard: standard text editing. `Enter` submits the surrounding form. Focus is visible as the accent border plus ring; in forced-colors mode it is a system outline.
- The placeholder never replaces the label.
- Click anywhere in the box (including padding) focuses the input. Clicking a decorative adornment does not; make interactive adornments real buttons with their own names.

#### Content

- Label: sentence case noun ("Workspace name"). Error: how to fix it ("Enter a complete email address.").
- Description: one short sentence, no exclamation marks.

#### Example

```tsx
<Input label="Workspace name" placeholder="e.g. Northwind" description="Visible to everyone." isRequired />
<Input label="Email" type="email" name="email" errorMessage="Enter a complete email address." isRequired />
<Input aria-label="Search orders" leading={<Icon icon={SearchIcon} />} trailing={<Kbd>/</Kbd>} />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Textarea: Several lines of text: `Textarea`.
- Instead, see Select: A choice from a list: `Select`, `RadioGroup`, `Checkbox`.
- Instead, see RadioGroup: A choice from a list: `Select`, `RadioGroup`, `Checkbox`.
- Instead, see Checkbox: A choice from a list: `Select`, `RadioGroup`, `Checkbox`.
- Renders: FieldMessages, Label

### Kbd

> A keyboard shortcut hint in mono type. With `keys` it renders `Mod` as the command symbol
on Apple platforms and as Ctrl elsewhere, and gives screen readers the spoken key names.

A keyboard shortcut hint in mono type. It renders a real `<kbd>` element.

- Import: `import { Kbd } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Kbd/Kbd.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Kbd`): Default, Apple, Windows, SingleKey, Arrows, WithChildren, InText, PortugueseLocale, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `readonly string[]` |  |  | The keys of one shortcut, in order: `['Mod', 'K']`, `['Shift', 'Enter']`, `['Esc']`. Recognized names (case-insensitive): `Mod` (Command on Apple, Control elsewhere), `Cmd`, `Meta`, `Ctrl`, `Shift`, `Alt`, `Option`, `Enter`, `Esc`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Space`, arrows (`Up`, `ArrowUp`, ...), `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`. Anything else is shown as typed (`K`, `/`, `1`). Symbols are hidden from assistive technology and replaced by the spoken name. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Free content shown as is (for example `⌘K`). Prefer `keys`, which is accessible and platform-aware. |
| `platform` | `'apple' \| 'other'` |  |  | Forces the platform used to render `Mod` and the modifier symbols. By default it is detected in the browser; during server rendering and the first client render it is `other` (Ctrl), then switches to `apple` (the command symbol) after hydration. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ name: (key: KbdKeyId) => string; label: (key: KbdKeyId) => string; }>` |  |  | Per-instance overrides of the spoken key names and short key labels. |

##### Inherited props

- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Kbd: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name(key: KbdKeyId)` |  |  |
| `label(key: KbdKeyId)` |  |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-caption`, `--ds-kbd-height`, `--ds-kbd-padding-inline`, `--ds-lh-caption`, `--ds-line-strong`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### When to use

- Next to a command, menu item or button to show its shortcut: "Search `Ctrl K`".
- In help text and tooltips that name a key.

#### When not to use

- To register the shortcut: use `useHotkey`. `Kbd` only displays it.
- For code or file names: use `<code>`.

#### Anatomy

```
kbd.root (border, mono)
  kbd.key   symbol or text   (aria-hidden when a spoken name replaces it)
            VisuallyHidden   spoken name ("Command")
  kbd.key   K
```

#### Platform awareness

`Mod` is Command on Apple platforms and Control elsewhere. The server and the first client render use `other` (Ctrl) so hydration matches; the component then reads the real platform (`useSyncExternalStore`) and re-renders with the command symbol on Apple devices. Pass `platform` to pin it. The same detection backs `useHotkey`, so the hint always matches the key that works.

On Apple platforms modifiers use symbols (`⌘ ⌃ ⇧ ⌥ ↵ ⎋ ⇥ ⌫ ⌦`); elsewhere they are short text (`Ctrl`, `Shift`, `Alt`, `Esc`, `Del`). Command and the arrows use their symbol everywhere.

#### Accessibility

- Screen readers do not reliably read symbols such as `⌘`. Every symbol or abbreviation is `aria-hidden` and followed by a visually hidden spoken name from the message catalog: "Command K", "Control Shift Escape".
- When the visible text already is the name (`Enter`, `Tab`) nothing is duplicated.
- The element has no role and is not focusable: it is text. The shortcut itself must be announced where it works (for example `aria-keyshortcuts` on the control, which is the control's responsibility).
- Text is `--ds-text-2`, which keeps at least 4.5:1 on the surface (the handoff used `--ds-text-3`).

#### Content rules

- Write the logical key (`Mod`), not the platform one.
- One `Kbd` per shortcut. A sequence ("G then I") is two `Kbd`s with the word between them from your own copy; sequences are not a built-in prop.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Kbd keys={['Mod', 'K']} />
<Kbd keys={['Shift', 'Enter']} />
<Kbd keys={['Esc']} />
```

#### Related components

- Renders: VisuallyHidden

### Label

> The visible label of a field. Must be rendered inside a React Aria field (TextField, Select,
CheckboxGroup, RadioGroup, ...), which wires `for` / `aria-labelledby`.
With `isRequired` it appends a visible marker (text from messages) that is hidden from
assistive technology: screen readers get "required" from the control itself (`required` /
`aria-required`), so announcing the marker too would repeat it.

Shared building blocks that make every form control (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`) look and behave the same: the same label, description and error styles, the same spacing, the same required marker, the same disabled treatment and the same validation timing. Tickets: ARCH-008, ARCH-009, part of GAP-003.

Most code never imports from `Field` directly: use the ready-made controls. Use the pieces when you compose a field that has no ready-made component yet (for example a custom picker built on a React Aria field).

- Import: `import { Label } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Field/Field.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Field`): Anatomy, ErrorsAfterSaveAttempt, RealtimeValidation

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `isRequired` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Adds the required marker after the text. The control itself must also be required. |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ requiredMark: string; }>` |  |  | Message overrides for this instance (`requiredMark`). |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLLabelElement>` |  |  |  |

##### Inherited props

- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `LabelProps` (react-aria-components): `elementType`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Field: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requiredMark` | `*` | Visible marker after the label of a required field. Hidden from assistive technology. |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-control-h-lg`, `--ds-control-h-md`, `--ds-control-h-sm`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-font-sans`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-md`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-text-3`, `--ds-weight-medium`

#### Exports

| Export                                 | What it is                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Label`                                | React Aria `Label` with the field label style (13/18, medium). `isRequired` appends the required marker.                                                         |
| `Description`                          | React Aria `Text slot="description"`, 13/18 in `--ds-text-3`. Linked to the control with `aria-describedby`.                                                     |
| `FieldError`                           | React Aria `FieldError`: renders only while the field is invalid and the error is displayed. The message is in a `role="alert"` element. 13/18 in `--ds-danger`. |
| `FieldMessages`                        | `Description` followed by `FieldError`. Every control renders it under its box.                                                                                  |
| `RequiredMark`                         | The marker alone, for fields whose label is not a `Label`.                                                                                                       |
| `FieldLabelingProps`, `WithLabel`      | Types. `FieldLabelingProps` makes "label, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`" mandatory. `WithLabel<P>` helps type stories.                                       |
| `FieldErrorMessage`, `FieldValidation` | Types for the `errorMessage` prop (a node or a function of the validation result).                                                                               |

#### Anatomy and spacing

```
Label                       13/18 medium, --ds-text
  gap: --ds-field-gap (6px)
Control box                 border --ds-line-control, radius md, height 32/40/48
  gap: --ds-field-gap
Description                 13/18, --ds-text-3
Error                       13/18, --ds-danger
```

The description stays visible when an error shows (the handoff replaced the hint with the error). Constraints such as "8 characters or more" remain useful while the user fixes the value, and both texts are linked to the control.

#### One state model (ARCH-009)

| State     | Look                                                                                                                       | Semantics                                          |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | `--ds-line-control` border, `--ds-bg` fill                                                                                 |                                                    |
| Hover     | Border brightens to `--ds-text-3`. The fill never changes, so the border stays at 3:1 or more.                             |                                                    |
| Focus     | Accent border and the 3px focus ring (`--ds-focus-ring`); forced-colors gets a system outline                              |                                                    |
| Invalid   | Danger border and danger focus ring                                                                                        | `aria-invalid`, error linked by `aria-describedby` |
| Read only | `--ds-surface` fill, same border                                                                                           | `readonly`; focusable, submitted with the form     |
| Disabled  | Label and control at `--ds-opacity-disabled`, dashed border, `--ds-surface` fill; description and error stay full strength | `disabled`; not focusable, not submitted           |
| Required  | Marker after the label                                                                                                     | `required` / `aria-required` on the control        |

Form-control borders use `--ds-line-control` and stay at 3:1 or better against the page in every state (WCAG 1.4.11). The suites assert this per state.

#### Required marker

`Label isRequired` appends the text of the `requiredMark` message (`*` by default) inside the label. The marker is `aria-hidden`: the control itself exposes "required", so announcing the marker too would repeat it. Override the text per instance (`messages={{ requiredMark: '(required)' }}`) or app-wide:

```tsx
<DSProvider locale="pt-BR" messages={{ Field: { requiredMark: '(obrigatório)' } }}>
```

#### Validation behavior: native (default), and why

React Aria fields validate in one of two modes:

- `validationBehavior="native"` (React Aria's default, kept here): the browser's constraint validation. Constraints such as `required`, `type`, `pattern` and `minLength` block submission. The error is **not displayed until the user tries to submit**; then focus moves to the first invalid field and the error appears. Custom `validate` rules report when the user commits the field (leaves it) and again on submit.
- `validationBehavior="aria"`: only ARIA attributes are set; nothing blocks submission, and the error follows every keystroke.

**Decision: `native` is the default for all fields.** It implements the product rule _errors appear only after a save attempt_ without extra code, it works without JavaScript hydration problems (the browser blocks the submit), it puts `required` on the real control and it moves focus to the first problem. `aria` suits fields that need live feedback (a username availability check, a counter): opt in per field with `validationBehavior="aria"`. A consumer that renders its own `Form` can set the mode for every field below it.

Rules for authors:

- Provide an `errorMessage` that says how to fix the problem ("Enter a complete email address."). Without one, React Aria shows the browser's own message, in the browser's language.
- To control `isInvalid` yourself (for example after a server response), pass `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`; the error shows at once.
- The error text is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`) and read again when focus lands on the field.
- Putting `<form>` in the page is enough; no wrapper component is required.

#### Accessibility

- Every control needs an accessible name: `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The types enforce it; a development warning covers untyped callers.
- `Description` and `FieldError` are linked with `aria-describedby`; the order is description, then error.
- Disabled fields are exempt from contrast requirements; everything else meets 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for borders.

#### Related components

- Used by: CheckboxGroup, Input, Radio, RadioGroup, Select, Textarea

### Link

> A link built on React Aria's `Link`. With `href` it renders a real `<a>` and uses the router
set on `DSProvider` for client-side navigation. Links that open a new tab (`target="_blank"`)
get `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, an external-link icon and a hidden note for screen readers.

A link to another page, section or site. Built on React Aria's `Link`: a real `<a href>` that uses the router set on `DSProvider` for client-side navigation.

- Handoff source: none (the handoff only had underlined `<a>` styles); part of GAP-002.

- Import: `import { Link } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Link/Link.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Link`): Default, InText, Standalone, External, Disabled, KeyboardActivation, Focused

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'inline' \| 'standalone'` |  | `'inline'` | - `inline` (default): underlined, for links inside running text. Color alone does not   identify a link (WCAG 1.4.1), so the underline is part of the design. - `standalone`: no underline at rest (underlined on hover and focus). Only where the context   makes it obvious that it is a link: a navigation list, a "View all" line under a heading. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Link text. Describe the destination or action ("Pricing details"), never "click here". |
| `messages` | `Partial<{ opensInNewTab: string; }>` |  |  | Override the built-in messages for this instance. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>` |  |  | Ref to the underlying `<a>` element. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`
- From `AriaLinkOptions` (react-aria): `isDisabled`
- From `AriaLinkProps` (react-aria): `aria-current`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `HoverEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onHoverChange`, `onHoverEnd`, `onHoverStart`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `LinkDOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `download`, `href`, `hrefLang`, `ping`, `referrerPolicy`, `rel`, `routerOptions`, `target`
- From `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `variant`: `inline`, `standalone`

#### Messages (i18n)

Locales shipped: en, pt-BR. Override per instance with the `messages` prop or globally with `<DSProvider messages={{ Link: { ... } }}>`.

| Key | English default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opensInNewTab` | `(opens in a new tab)` |  |

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radius-sm`, `--ds-space-1`

#### When to use

- To go somewhere: another route, a section (`#id`), a document or an external site.
- Inside running text (`inline`), or as a quiet navigation line such as "View all orders" (`standalone`).

#### When not to use

- To run an action in place (save, delete, open a dialog): use `Button`.
- For a styled call to action that happens to navigate: still a link semantically, but use a `Button` with `href` when it is the primary action of the screen (planned with the button-as-link variant).

#### Variants

| Variant      | At rest   | Hover and keyboard focus | Use                                                                      |
| ------------ | --------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `inline`     | underline | thicker underline        | Links inside sentences. Default.                                         |
| `standalone` | none      | underline                | Navigation lists, "View all" lines. Only where context makes it obvious. |

Color alone never identifies a link (WCAG 1.4.1), so inline links are always underlined. The accent color (`--ds-accent`) is reserved for focus, selection and links.

#### Routing

Wrap the app once: `<DSProvider navigate={router.push} useHref={router.resolve}>`. Links with a relative `href` then navigate without a page reload; modified clicks (Ctrl/Cmd, middle button) and `target="_blank"` keep the browser behavior.

#### Accessibility

- Real `<a href>`: opens in a new tab with the context menu, can be copied, works without JavaScript.
- Keys: `Tab` focuses, `Enter` follows. (`Space` does not activate a link, by design.)
- Focus: 3px accent ring through `data-focus-visible`; forced-colors mode repaints the transparent outline and system link colors apply.
- Links that open a new tab: the name ends with "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers (hidden text from the `Link` messages) and a decorative icon shows it visually. `rel="noopener noreferrer"` is added automatically.
- Contrast: accent `#8AB4FF` on the dark surfaces is well above 4.5:1.
- Target size: inline links in text are exempt from WCAG 2.5.8; standalone links should sit in a 24px-high row.
- Reduced motion: hover changes decoration thickness only, no animation.

#### Content rules

- Link text describes the destination or action and makes sense out of context: "Pricing details", "Download invoice". Never "click here" or "read more".
- Sentence case, no trailing punctuation inside the link, no emoji.
- Do not repeat the word "link". The role is announced.

#### Examples

```tsx
<p>
  Read the <Link href="/pricing">pricing details</Link> before you change a plan.
</p>

<Link variant="standalone" href="/orders">View all orders</Link>

<Link href="https://example.com/docs" target="_blank">Documentation</Link>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Button: To run an action in place (save, delete, open a dialog): use `Button`.
- Renders: Icon, VisuallyHidden

### Meter

> A bar that shows a quantity within a known range (disk used, quota, score), as opposed to
progress of a task. Built on React Aria `Meter` (`role="meter"`).

A thin bar (4 px) with a label and a value in mono type. `Progress` shows the progress of a task, determinate or indeterminate (React Aria `ProgressBar`, `role="progressbar"`). `Meter` shows a quantity within a range (React Aria `Meter`, `role="meter"`) and shares the same look.

- Import: `import { Meter } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/Progress/Progress.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/Progress`): Default, WithoutLabel, ShowValue, Empty, Complete, Warning, Danger, Indeterminate, AllTones, AsMeter, RightToLeft

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label, wired to the bar with `aria-labelledby`. Required unless you set `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`: a bar without a name is an accessibility bug (React Aria warns in development). |
| `meta` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Text on the right of the label, in mono type: "6.2 / 10 GB". It is visual only. If it says more than the percentage, also pass `valueLabel` so screen readers hear the same thing. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` |  |  | Shows the formatted percentage (`62%`, from `Intl` with the active locale) as `meta` when `meta` is not given. |
| `tone` | `'accent' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` |  | `'accent'` | Color of the fill. Color is never the only signal: pair it with a label or `meta`. Default `accent`. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  |  |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `ProgressBarBaseProps` (react-aria): `formatOptions`, `maxValue`, `minValue`, `value`, `valueLabel`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Variants, sizes and tones

- `tone`: `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration-progress`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-font-mono`, `--ds-fs-label`, `--ds-lh-label`, `--ds-progress-height`, `--ds-progress-indeterminate-duration`, `--ds-progress-indeterminate-width`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-space-2`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-success`, `--ds-surface-hover`, `--ds-text-2`, `--ds-warning`

#### When to use

- `Progress`: an upload, an import, a multi-step job. Use indeterminate when the amount is unknown.
- `Meter`: disk used, quota consumed, a score. The value is a measurement, not a task that will finish.

#### When not to use

- Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
- Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.

#### Anatomy

```
div[role=progressbar|meter]
  div.header      Label (left) · meta (right, mono)
  div.track       4px, pill
    div.fill      width = percentage (or a sweeping segment when indeterminate)
```

#### Accessibility

- The bar is named by the visible label (`aria-labelledby`) or `aria-label`; React Aria warns in development when a bar has neither.
- `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are set, and `aria-valuetext` is the percentage formatted with `Intl` for the active locale ("62%", "62,5%" in pt-BR). If you show "6.2 / 10 GB", set `valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB"` so screen readers hear the same thing.
- An indeterminate bar has no `aria-valuenow`, so assistive technology reports it as busy without a number.
- Progress does not announce changes by itself. For long tasks, announce milestones and completion in a live region (for example with a `Toast`).
- Color is not the only signal: the label and the value text carry the meaning. The fill is 4 px high but the track and fill are a graphic that keeps at least 3:1 against the surface; the track is a neutral surface step.
- **Reduced motion:** the width change has no transition and the indeterminate sweep becomes a static segment centered in the track. **Forced colors:** the track gets a border and the fill uses the text color.

#### Content rules

- Labels are nouns or short phrases in sentence case ("Storage", "Importing orders").
- Put units and ratios in `meta`, in the formatted form of the active locale.

#### Examples

```tsx
<Progress value={62} label="Storage" meta="6.2 / 10 GB" valueLabel="6.2 of 10 GB" />
<Progress isIndeterminate label="Importing orders" />
<Meter value={82} tone="warning" label="Quota" showValue />
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Spinner: Waiting with no known structure and no label: use `Spinner`.
- Instead, see Skeleton: Content that is loading: use `Skeleton`.

### Progress

> A thin bar for a task that makes progress: determinate with a `value`, or indeterminate
when the amount is unknown. Built on React Aria `ProgressBar` (`role="progressbar"`).
For a measured quantity that is not a task (disk used, quota) use `Meter`.

A thin bar (4 px) with a label and a value in mono type. `Progress` shows the progress of a task, determinate or indeterminate (React Aria `ProgressBar`, `role="progressbar"`). `Meter` shows a quantity within a range (React Aria `Meter`, `role="meter"`) and shares the same look.

- Import: `import { Progress } from '@loui/ds';`

| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  |  |

### Radio

> One option of a `RadioGroup`. `value` is required and identifies the option.

A labelled set of mutually exclusive options with native radio inputs. Built on React Aria `RadioGroup` + `RadioField` + `RadioButton` (the non-deprecated pair that supports a description per option). Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md).

- Import: `import { Radio } from '@loui/ds';`
- Status: experimental (do not use in recipes until stable)
- Source: `src/components/RadioGroup/RadioGroup.tsx`
- Stories (Storybook title `Components/RadioGroup`): Default, WithSelection, Horizontal, WithDescriptions, Required, Invalid, Disabled, DisabledOption, ReadOnly, LongLabels

#### Props

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Secondary text under the label. Linked with `aria-describedby`, not part of the name. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  | Class name for the option root. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  | Ref to the option root `<div>`. Use `inputRef` for the `<input>`. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Visible label. Prefer it: sighted and assistive technology users see the same name. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  | Accessible name when there is no visible label (for example a search box with an icon). |
| `aria-labelledby` | `string` |  |  | Id of the element that names the field. |

##### Inherited props

- From `AriaLabelingProps` (@react-types/shared): `aria-describedby`, `aria-details`
- From `DOMProps` (@react-types/shared): `id`
- From `DOMRenderProps` (react-aria-components): `render`
- From `FocusableProps` (@react-types/shared): `autoFocus`
- From `FocusEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onBlur`, `onFocus`, `onFocusChange`
- From `KeyboardEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`
- From `PressEvents` (@react-types/shared): `onClick`, `onPress`, `onPressChange`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressStart`, `onPressUp`
- From `RadioFieldProps` (react-aria-components): `inputRef`
- From `RadioProps` (react-aria): `isDisabled`, `value`
- From `SlotProps` (react-aria-components): `slot`
- Standard DOM attributes, ARIA attributes and event handlers; other attributes and `ref` go to the root element.

#### Design tokens used

`--ds-accent`, `--ds-bg`, `--ds-danger`, `--ds-duration`, `--ds-ease`, `--ds-field-choice-gap`, `--ds-focus-ring`, `--ds-focus-ring-danger`, `--ds-fs-small`, `--ds-lh-small`, `--ds-line-control`, `--ds-opacity-disabled`, `--ds-radio-dot-size`, `--ds-radio-size`, `--ds-radius-pill`, `--ds-space-1`, `--ds-space-3`, `--ds-space-5`, `--ds-target-min`, `--ds-text`, `--ds-text-3`

#### When to use

- Choose exactly one of 2 to 5 options that users want to compare.

#### When not to use

- Many options: `Select`.
- Independent choices: `Checkbox`.
- Immediate on/off: `Switch`.

#### Props (key ones)

`RadioGroup`:

| Prop                                                  | Notes                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                                               | Group name. Required: pass `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (type error otherwise; development warning too). |
| `description`, `errorMessage`                         | Linked to the group by `aria-describedby`.                                                                             |
| `orientation`                                         | `vertical` (default) or `horizontal`.                                                                                  |
| `value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange(value)`          | React Aria naming; `value` is a string.                                                                                |
| `name`                                                | Shared by every radio; the selected value is submitted.                                                                |
| `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly` | Standard states.                                                                                                       |

`Radio`: `value` (required), `label`, `description`, `isDisabled`, `className`, `inputRef`.

#### Look

- 18px circle (`--ds-radio-size`), `--ds-line-control` border at 3:1 or better in every state, accent border and a 9px accent dot when selected. Hover brightens the border.
- The option row is at least 24px tall and the whole row is clickable.
- A disabled group dims once; a single disabled option uses `--ds-opacity-disabled`.

#### Accessibility and keyboard

| Key                        | Behavior                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                      | One tab stop: lands on the selected radio, or the first one when nothing is selected            |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowRight` | Next radio, selects it, wraps from the last to the first (directions follow the text direction) |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowLeft`    | Previous radio, selects it, wraps                                                               |
| `Space`                    | Selects the focused radio                                                                       |

Roving focus is handled by React Aria, so only one radio is in the tab order (the handoff made every radio tabbable). `role="radiogroup"` is named by the label; the description and error belong to the group; `aria-required` and `aria-invalid` are set.

#### Example

```tsx
<RadioGroup
  label="Region"
  name="region"
  defaultValue="eu"
  description="You cannot change this later."
>
  <Radio value="eu" label="EU: Frankfurt" />
  <Radio value="us" label="US: Virginia" description="Default for new workspaces." />
</RadioGroup>
```

#### Related components

- Instead, see Select: Many options: `Select`.
- Instead, see Checkbox: Independent choices: `Checkbox`.
- Instead, see Switch: Immediate on/off: `Switch`.
- Renders: Description, FieldMessages, Label

### RadioGroup

> A labelled `role="radiogroup"` of mutually exclusive options with native radio inputs.
The group is one tab stop; arrow keys move and select (roving focus is handled by React Aria).
`value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange(value)` follow React Aria; `name` is shared by every radio.
A group needs a name: pass `label`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

A labelled set of mutually exclusive options with native radio inputs. Built on React Aria `RadioGroup` + `RadioField` + `RadioButton` (the non-deprecated pair that supports a description per option). Shared field behavior is in [Field](../Field/Field.md).
